title_en: 浙江省食品有限公司诉上海市泰康食品有限公司、浙江永康四路火腿一厂商标侵权纠纷案
ruling_gist_en: For a registered trademark containing a geographical name formed due to historical reasons, although the trademark owner enjoys the exclusive right to use the trademark under the Trademark Law, if the geographical name has been approved by the specialized national administrative authority for the implementation of protection of products of a specific geographical origin, then the civil subjects authorized to use such designation may use the special mark of geographical origin within the statutory scope. Where the trademark owner files a lawsuit with the People's Court on the ground that the lawful use of the special mark of geographical origin by the actor infringes upon its exclusive right to use the trademark, and requests compensation for infringement, the People's Court shall not support such claim.
keywords_en: Civil; trademark infringement dispute; first instance; Intermediate People's Court; Zhejiang Province; Shanghai City; legal person; Trademark Law; conflict between exclusive right to use a registered trademark and the mark of protected geographical origin; scope of protection of a registered trademark containing a geographical name; defense of fair use; rejection of claims; trademark infringement; Jinhua ham; protection of products of specific geographical origin; trademark formed due to historical reasons; good faith; trademark right; trademark infringement dispute of Silu Ham No.1 Factory
full_text_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Food Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Taikang Food Co., Ltd. and Zhejiang Yongkang Silu Ham Factory No. 1

— Dispute over Trademark Infringement

【Ruling Summary】

For a registered trademark containing a place name formed due to historical reasons, although the trademark owner enjoys the exclusive right to use the trademark under the Trademark Law, if the place name has been approved by a specialized state administrative authority for the implementation of protection of products of geographical origin, then civil subjects authorized to use it may use the special sign for products of geographical origin within the statutory scope. Where the trademark owner files a lawsuit with the people's court on the grounds that the lawful use by an actor of the special sign for products of geographical origin infringes upon its trademark exclusive right, and requests compensation for damages, the people's court shall not support such claim.

Plaintiff: Zhejiang Provincial Food Co., Ltd., domiciled at: Zhongshan Middle Road, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Zhao Xiaoyu, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Defendant: Shanghai Taikang Food Co., Ltd., domiciled at: East Jinling Road, Huangpu District, Shanghai.
Legal Representative: Zou Jianguo, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Zhejiang Yongkang Silu Ham Factory No. 1, domiciled at: Longshan Town, Yongkang City, Zhejiang Province.
Legal Representative: Fang Xiqian, Factory Director.

The plaintiff, Zhejiang Provincial Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zheshi Company), filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendants, Shanghai Taikang Food Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Taikang Company) and Zhejiang Yongkang Silu Ham Factory No. 1 (hereinafter referred to as Yongkang Ham Factory), over a dispute concerning trademark infringement.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff is the owner of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "金华火腿" (Jinhua Ham). This registered trademark consists of the words "金华火腿" within a square frame resembling a seal, forming a distinctive visual mark. In 1986, with the approval of the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the State Trademark Office), the plaintiff made appropriate changes to the specific style of use of its registered trademark on the surface of the ham, but such use has the same legal effect as the registered trademark. In July 2003, at the store of Defendant Taikang Company located at No. 776 East Nanjing Road, Shanghai, the plaintiff discovered that the ham being sold by the defendant used the plaintiff's registered trademark "金华火腿". The plaintiff then sent a letter to Taikang Company, informing it that "金华火腿" is the plaintiff's registered trademark and requesting it to stop selling the infringing goods. In September of the same year, the plaintiff again found at Defendant Taikang Company's store that the ham it sold bore the words "金华火腿" and was produced by Yongkang Ham Factory. According to investigations, three out of four ham-selling companies on the East Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street in Shanghai sold hams from Yongkang Ham Factory, with sales in 2003 exceeding 30,000 pieces. The plaintiff has never licensed Yongkang Ham Factory to use the "金华火腿" trademark. Therefore, Yongkang Ham Factory's unauthorized use of the words "金华火腿" on the ham surface infringed upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark. Defendant Taikang Company, knowing that the goods it sold infringed upon another person's exclusive right to use a registered trademark, also constituted infringement of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark. Hence, the plaintiff requested the court to order: 1. Taikang Company to immediately cease selling the infringing goods and publicly apologize to the plaintiff; 2. Yongkang Ham Factory to cease producing infringing goods identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark and publicly apologize to the plaintiff; 3. Yongkang Ham Factory to, within 30 days, remove from its hams the signs identical or similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark, and to confiscate the "金华火腿" skin stamps it had made without authorization; 4. The two defendants to jointly compensate the plaintiff RMB 50,000, with joint and several liability; 5. The two defendants to jointly compensate the plaintiff for notarization expenses of RMB 2,000, the cost of purchasing the infringing ham at the time of notarization of RMB 165, and attorney fees of RMB 10,000.

The plaintiff, Zheshi Company, submitted the following evidence:
1. The Trademark Registration Certificate, Certificate of Approval for Change of Name of Registrant, Certificate of Approval for Change of Address of Registrant, and Certificate of Approval for Renewal of Registration, to prove that Zheshi Company is the lawful owner of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark "金华火腿";
2. The Reply of the State Trademark Office [1986] Gongshang Biao Zong Zi No. 165, "Reply Concerning the Use of the '金华' Ham Trademark", to prove that the State Trademark Office approved Zheshi Company's appropriate changes to the specific style of use of its registered trademark on the ham surface, and that such use has the same legal effect as the registered trademark;
3. The Approval of the State Trademark Office, Trademark Case Document No. [2004] 64, "Approval Concerning the Proper Use of the Words '金华火腿'", to prove that the trademark "金华火腿" used on ham goods in Class 29 of the International Classification of Goods and Services for the Purposes of the Registration of Marks is the registered trademark of Zheshi Company;
4. Four Certificates of Zhejiang Province Famous Trademark, to prove that in August 1992, October 1997, March 2001, and January 2004, the Zhejiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce successively recognized Zheshi Company's "金华火腿" trademark as a Zhejiang Province Famous Trademark;
5. The letter, mail tracking receipt, and reply receipt sent by Zheshi Company to Defendant Taikang Company, to prove the fact that Zheshi Company requested the defendant to cease selling the infringing goods;
6. Evidence such as the notarized record of the plaintiff, Zheshi Company, purchasing ham from Defendant Taikang Company, the product pattern of the plaintiff, the "General Requirements for Products of Geographical Origin", the invoice for the ham purchase, the invoice for notarization fees, and the invoice for attorney fees, to prove that the plaintiff's claimed amount for the defendants' infringement liability has a reasonable basis.

Defendant Taikang Company's Defense:
1. Before selling the products of Defendant Yongkang Ham Factory, Taikang Company had already inspected and verified the outer packaging, trademarks, etc., and confirmed that the trademark "真方宗" marked on the outer packaging is a registered trademark of Yongkang Ham Factory, and that the geographical origin name and sign used were approved by the relevant state functional departments.
2. "金华火腿" is a well-known product name. The "金华火腿" sold by Taikang Company originates from the Jinhua region and would not mislead consumers or cause harm to consumers.
3. The store of Taikang Company enjoys the reputation of a "China Time-honored Brand", and "金华火腿" is a traditional product it has operated. Therefore, it requested the court to reject the claims of the plaintiff, Zheshi Company.

Defendant Yongkang Ham Factory's Defense:
1. The trademark mark of the plaintiff, Zheshi Company, is "金华" (Jinhua), not "金华火腿". The trademark mark on the plaintiff's Trademark Registration Certificate is "金华", and the Trademark Registration Certificate is the sole legal document proving the scope of protection of the plaintiff's trademark rights. On its own website, the plaintiff explicitly states its registered trademark as the "金华" brand. This fact has also been confirmed by the effective civil judgments of (2003) Hang Min San Chu Zi No. 110 and (2004) Zhe Min San Zhong Zi No. 154. The State Trademark Office's consent for the plaintiff to use the words "金华火腿" on its products was based on the description of special processing technical requirements in the plaintiff's relevant request. The State Trademark Office merely permitted the plaintiff to use the words "金华火腿" on the ham surface, but such non-standard use cannot oppose the proper use by others.
2. "金华火腿" is the name of a product of geographical origin. The defendant's use of this name does not infringe upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use the registered trademark. Relevant announcements from state ministries and national standards clearly state that "金华火腿" is the name of a product of geographical origin, and any manufacturer that fulfills certain legal procedures may use this name. Fifty-five enterprises, including the defendant, have been approved to use the name of geographical origin product "金华火腿". The defendant's current use of this name on its hams is approved by the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine (hereinafter referred to as AQSIQ) and the Jinhua Ham Product of Geographical Origin Protection Committee, and is strictly used in accordance with national mandatory standards.
3. The defendant's use of "金华" constitutes fair use. (1) "金华" is an administrative geographical name. When describing products originating from the Jinhua region, only by referencing "金华" can the origin of the product be correctly expressed. (2) "火腿" (ham) is a generic product name, and the plaintiff has no right to prohibit others from using it. The defendant's addition of the words "金华" before "火腿" is intended to indicate the product's quality, origin, and to provide consumers with purchasing guidance. (3) The defendant's use is made in good faith, conforming to the principle of good faith. In its use, the defendant has not intentionally highlighted or exaggerated parts identical or similar to the plaintiff's trademark so as to cause consumer confusion.
4. "金华火腿" is a distinctive name of a well-known product. "金华火腿" has a history of over 1,200 years and was widely used as early as the 17th century, gaining social acceptance and recognition. It is a classic case of prior use. Furthermore, allowing the defendant to use "金华火腿" serves to maximize social benefits.
5. The defendant has no subjective intent to infringe upon the plaintiff's registered trademark. The defendant's purpose in using "金华火腿" is to indicate to consumers that the product is produced in Jinhua and is genuine "金华火腿", with no subjective intent to infringe. In summary, the defendant requested the court to reject the plaintiff's claims.

Defendants Taikang Company and Yongkang Ham Factory submitted the following evidence:
1. The request of Zhejiang Provincial Food Company, "Request Concerning the Trademark Affairs of '金华' Ham", to prove that the State Trademark Office only permitted the plaintiff, Zheshi Company, to use the words "金华火腿" on the ham surface, and did not confer on the words "金华火腿" used on the ham by the plaintiff the same legal effect as its registered trademark.
2. The Civil Judgment (2003) Hang Min San Chu Zi No. 110 of Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province and the Civil Judgment (2004) Zhe Min San Zhong Zi No. 154 of the Zhejiang Higher People's Court, to prove that Zheshi Company's registered trademark has been confirmed as the "金华" brand by effective civil judgments.
3. Some of Zheshi Company's award certificates, pictures of hams from Yongkang Ham Factory sold by Taikang Company, award certificates of Yongkang Ham Factory, AQSIQ Announcement No. 84 of 2002, AQSIQ Announcement No. 87 of 2003, "Product of Geographical Origin — Jinhua Ham", "Management Measures for the Protection of Jinhua Ham as a Product of Geographical Origin", Product of Geographical Origin Quality Responsibility Letter, License for the Use of Special Signs for Products of Geographical Origin, Trademark Registration Certificate for the "真方宗" brand, Certification of Naming, etc., to prove that Yongkang Ham Factory uses the registered trademark "真方宗", that "金华火腿" is the name of a product of geographical origin, and that numerous local enterprises in Jinhua have been approved to use the name of geographical origin product "金华火腿".

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court found the following upon trial:

In October 1979, Pujiang County Food Company of Zhejiang Province applied for and obtained the registration of Trademark No. 130131 in Class 33 (ham). Subsequently, the class of goods was converted from Class 33 to Class 29 of the International Classification. The Trademark Registration Certificate records the mark as "Trademark Jinhua Brand". Below the words is a rectangular pattern with a red background. Within the pattern is a square box composed of decorative lines. At the top of the square box are the words "Develop the Economy, Ensure Supply", in the middle are the words "金华火腿", and at the bottom are the words "Pujiang County Food Company". At the lower right corner of this rectangular red paper are the following words: "Note: 'Develop the Economy, Ensure Supply', company name, and decoration are not within the scope of exclusive use." On March 14, 1983, this trademark was approved for assignment to Zhejiang Provincial Food Company. On October 7, 2000, the trademark registrant was changed to the plaintiff, Zheshi Company. In December 2002, the trademark was renewed, with the validity period from March 1, 2003, to February 28, 2013. On August 21, 1986, Zhejiang Provincial Food Company submitted to the State Trademark Office the "Request Concerning the Trademark Affairs of '金华' Ham" (Shi Ye [1986] No. 174) (hereinafter referred to as the "Request"), proposing: "Hereafter, all packaging materials, product certificates, etc., bearing the '金华' ham trademark, as well as the promotion and advertising of the '金华' ham trademark, except for removing the parts 'Develop the Economy, Ensure Supply' and 'Pujiang County Food Company', shall use the mark as approved in the Registration Certificate for the '金华' ham trademark, and shall indicate 'Registered Trademark' or the registration mark; due to the characteristics of the processing technique, the font and arrangement position of the words '金华火腿' directly stamped on the ham shall continue to follow the historically used style, but without indicating 'Registered Trademark' or the registration mark, so as to distinguish it from the registered mark approved in the Registration Certificate." In September of the same year, the State Trademark Office issued the "Reply Concerning the Use of the '金华' Ham Trademark" ([1986] Gongshang Biao Zong Zi No. 165) (hereinafter referred to as the "Reply"), agreeing to the method of use proposed in Zhejiang Provincial Food Company's Shi Ye [1986] No. 174 Request.

On the surface of the hams it produces and sells, the plaintiff, Zheshi Company, marks "Supervised by Zhejiang Provincial Food Co., Ltd.", "金华火腿", the production unit number, and the production date code. On March 9, 2004, the State Trademark Office issued the "Approval Concerning the Proper Use of the Words '金华火腿'" (Trademark Case Document No. [2004] 64) (hereinafter referred to as the "Approval"), stating that the trademark "金华火腿" used on ham goods in Class 29 of the International Classification of Goods and Services for the Purposes of the Registration of Marks is the registered trademark of Zheshi Company; "金华特产火腿" (Jinhua specialty ham), "×× (Trademark) 金华火腿", and "金华 ×× (Trademark) 火腿" fall within the scope of proper use as described in Article 49 of the Regulations for the Implementation of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Implementation Regulations); furthermore, in actual use, the above proper use methods should have a consistent direction of text arrangement, and identical font, size, and color, and shall not highlight the words "金华火腿".

In August 1992, October 1997, March 2001, and January 2004, the Zhejiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce successively recognized the plaintiff Zheshi Company's "金华火腿" trademark as a Zhejiang Province Famous Trademark. Gold Medal Certificates issued to Zhejiang Provincial Food Company by the National Quality Award Review Committee in December 1985, Zhejiang Famous Brand Product Certificates issued to Zhejiang Provincial Food Company by multiple units including the Zhejiang Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce in August 1993, and Zhejiang Famous Brand Product Certificates issued to Zhejiang Provincial Food Company by the People's Government of Zhejiang Province in August 1998, among others, describe the plaintiff's award-winning product as "Jinhua Brand" Jinhua Ham or "Jinhua Brand" Extra Grade Jinhua Ham. In September 2001, a Zhejiang Famous Brand Product Certificate issued to Zhejiang Provincial Food Co., Ltd. by the Zhejiang Famous Brand Product Certification Committee described the plaintiff's award-winning product as "Jinhua Brand" Ham. The Civil Judgment (2003) Hang Min San Chu Zi No. 110 of Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province and the Civil Judgment (2004) Zhe Min San Zhong Zi No. 154 of the Zhejiang Higher People's Court described the plaintiff's trademark as the "Jinhua Brand" and the "金华" (Jinhua) ham registered trademark.

On August 17, 1999, the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision promulgated and implemented the "Regulations on the Protection of Products of Geographical Origin". Article 2 of these Regulations states: "The term 'product of geographical origin' as used in these Regulations refers to a product produced within a specific region using raw materials from that specific region, processed according to traditional techniques within that specific region, whose quality, characteristics, or reputation are essentially attributable to the geographical features of its origin, and which is named by reference to the geographical origin upon examination and approval in accordance with these Regulations." Article 16 states: "After a producer's application is registered by the Protection Office, it may use the special sign for products of geographical origin on its products and obtain protection for the product of geographical origin." On December 7, 1999, the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision issued the National Standard of the People's Republic of China, "General Requirements for Products of Geographical Origin". Subsection 6.4 of this standard, regarding labels, states: "The contents of labels for products of geographical origin, in addition to complying with relevant state regulations, shall also specify special marking contents, such as the name of the geographical origin, the name and address of the raw material supplier, and shall use the special sign for products of geographical origin." Subsection 7.1 of this standard specifies that the special sign for products of geographical origin "has an elliptical outline, a gray outer ring, a green background, with a red map of the People's Republic of China in the center of the ellipse, and a gray Great Wall at the bottom of the ellipse. The words 'Product of Geographical Origin of the People's Republic of China' are marked on the upper part of the ellipse, in black Zongyi typeface." On August 28, 2002, AQSIQ issued Announcement No. 84 of 2002, passing the examination of the application for protection of "Jinhua Ham" as a product of geographical origin, and approving the implementation of protection for Jinhua Ham as a product of geographical origin from the date of the announcement. On April 24, 2003, AQSIQ issued the National Standard of the People's Republic of China, "Product of Geographical Origin — Jinhua Ham". Subsection 5.3.3 of this standard states: "Jinhua Ham shall be salted between the beginning of winter of the current year and the beginning of spring of the following year, with a total period from salting to fermentation until reaching maturity of not less than 9 months." Subsection 8.1.1 states: "The marking of sales packaging products shall be implemented in accordance with GB7718 (General Standard for Food Labeling), indicating the following: the name of the product of geographical origin Jinhua Ham, product standard number, name and address of the producer, net content, production date, shelf life, quality grade, and the special sign for a product of geographical origin of the People's Republic of China shall be indicated in a conspicuous position on the sales packaging of Jinhua Ham." On September 24, 2003, AQSIQ issued Announcement No. 87 of 2003, passing the examination of applications from 55 enterprises, including Zhejiang Changshan County Ham Company and the defendant Yongkang Ham Factory, for the use of the special sign for the product of geographical origin Jinhua Ham, and granting registration. From that date, the aforementioned 55 enterprises may use the special sign for the product of geographical origin "Jinhua Ham" on their products in accordance with relevant regulations and obtain protection for the product of geographical origin.

In 1995, the China Special Product Hometown Naming and Publicity Activity Organizing Committee designated Jinhua City, Zhejiang Province as the "Hometown of Chinese Jinhua Ham." On December 9, 2002, the General Office of Jinhua Municipal People's Government and the General Office of Quzhou Municipal People's Government issued (JZB [2002] No. 94) the "Administrative Measures for the Protection of Jinhua Ham as a Product of Origin (Trial)." Article 5 of these Measures stipulates: "Any unit or individual that uses the special mark for Jinhua Ham as a product of origin must apply through the prescribed procedures and, after registration with the Product of Origin Protection Office of the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine, may use the mark on its products"; Article 9 stipulates: "The special mark for the protection of Jinhua Ham as a product of origin consists of the special mark pattern for products of origin as prescribed by national standards and the words 'Jinhua Ham.' The special mark may be printed directly on packaging or instructions, or used in enterprise product introductions"; Article 12 stipulates: "Holders of the 'Certificate for Use of the Special Mark for Jinhua Ham as a Product of Origin' whose hams meet the requirements of the national mandatory standards for Jinhua Ham have the right to use the special mark for Jinhua Ham as a product of origin on labels, packaging, and advertising instructions of the Jinhua Ham they produce, and to obtain protection as a product of origin; they have the right to stamp on the skin of the Jinhua Ham they produce the words 'XX Brand Jinhua Ham, Certified by the Origin Management Committee,' and the stamp for these words shall be uniformly issued and managed by the Jinhua Ham Management Committee." On April 21, 2003, the defendant Yongkang Ham Factory registered the trademark "真方宗" for use on goods in Class 29 (ham, meat, etc.) as approved, with a validity period until April 20, 2013. In June of the same year, Yongkang Ham Factory was rated by the Jinhua Ham Industry Association as one of the first "Jinhua Ham Star Enterprises." On October 16, 2003, the Jinhua Ham Product of Origin Protection Management Committee issued to Yongkang Ham Factory the "Certificate for Use of the Special Mark for Jinhua Ham as a Product of Origin," with certificate number Jinyuanbao (2003) No. 12. On November 12 of the same year, Yongkang Ham Factory signed the "Quality Responsibility Letter for Jinhua Ham as a Product of Origin" with the Jinhua Quality and Technical Supervision and Testing Center.

On July 27, 2003, the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company sent a letter to the defendant Taikang Company, stating that "Jinhua Ham" is the plaintiff's registered trademark and requiring it to immediately cease selling hams that infringe the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark, failing which legal action would be taken. On October 14, 2003, the plaintiff's agent ad litem, Zhang Feng, purchased one "真方宗" brand ham from Taikang Company. The outer packaging of the ham bore the words "真方宗," "真方宗火腿," "Jinhua Ham Star Enterprise," and the name, factory address, and telephone number of the defendant Yongkang Ham Factory; the skin of the ham bore the words "真方宗牌," "Jinhua Ham," and "Certified by the Origin Management Committee"; the date of manufacture was August 30, 2003. Upon the plaintiff's application for preservation of evidence, the Shanghai Notary Public Office notarized the above purchase process and issued Notarial Certificate (2003) Hu Zheng Jing No. 5829, which was accompanied by photos of the purchased ham and a copy of the sales invoice from the defendant Taikang Company.

On November 20, 2003, the Shanghai No. 1 Intermediate People's Court, upon the plaintiff's application, preserved evidence of the defendant Taikang Company's sales, seizing one ham sold by Taikang Company and some sales invoices.

In this case, the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company incurred notary fees of RMB 2,000, RMB 165 for the ham purchased during notarization, and attorney fees of RMB 10,000.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. The scope of protection of the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company's exclusive right to use its registered trademark; 2. Whether the acts of the defendants Taikang Company and Yongkang Ham Factory infringed the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark.

The Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court held:

1. Regarding the scope of protection of the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company's exclusive right to use its registered trademark.

The plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company argued: The scope of protection of the plaintiff's registered trademark is "Jinhua Ham." "Jinhua Brand" is the designation for this registered trademark. Based on the annotation in the lower right corner of the registration certificate, excluding "Develop Economy, Ensure Supply," the enterprise name, and decorative content, the scope of protection of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark is "Jinhua Ham." In its Reply Letter, the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce agreed to allow the plaintiff to make appropriate changes to the specific form of use of its registered trademark on ham skin, and this Reply Letter has the same legal probative force as the registered trademark. Moreover, the Official Reply of the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce and the Zhejiang Provincial Famous Trademark Certificate also clearly indicate that the plaintiff's trademark is the "Jinhua Ham" trademark. The defendants Taikang Company and Yongkang Ham Factory argued: The scope of protection of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark is "Jinhua," not "Jinhua Ham." The plaintiff's trademark registration certificate states that the plaintiff's trademark is "Jinhua Brand." In its Request for Instructions, Zhejiang Provincial Food Company also referred to its own trademark as the "Jinhua" ham trademark. Some of the plaintiff's honor certificates, the plaintiff's own website materials, and relevant court judgments also refer to the plaintiff's trademark as "Jinhua Brand" or "Jinhua" trademark.

First, according to the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Trademark Law), the exclusive right to use registered trademarks of citizens, legal persons, and other organizations is protected by Chinese law. The exclusive right to use a registered trademark is limited to the trademark approved for registration by the trademark administrative department and the goods for which it is approved for use. The plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company's registered trademark with Certificate No. 130131 was registered with the trademark administrative department and, having been duly renewed, remains valid, and the exclusive right to use this registered trademark is protected by Chinese law.

Second, regarding the scope of protection of the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company's exclusive right to use its registered trademark, it should be determined based on the historical context at the time of trademark registration and the content recorded in the trademark registration certificate. The plaintiff's trademark registration certificate is an integral whole. The trademark was registered in the late 1970s, when the format of registered trademarks and trademark registration certificates was significantly different from the present, but this does not change the scope of protection of the exclusive right to use the trademark. The annotation in the lower right corner of the plaintiff's trademark registration certificate clearly excludes "'Develop Economy, Ensure Supply,' the enterprise name, and decorative content" from the scope of exclusive use. The Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce, as the competent authority for trademark registration and management in China, also clarified in its Official Reply that the plaintiff's registered trademark is the "Jinhua Ham" trademark.

In conclusion, the core of the scope of protection of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark is "Jinhua Ham." The defendant Yongkang Ham Factory's argument that the scope of protection of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark is merely "Jinhua" is inconsistent with the facts and is not supported by this court.

2. Regarding whether the acts of the defendants Taikang Company and Yongkang Ham Factory infringed the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company's exclusive right to use its registered trademark.

The plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company argued: The plaintiff's stamping of "Jinhua Ham" on the skin of the hams it produces is an extension of the use of its registered trademark and has the same legal effect as the registered trademark. The defendant Yongkang Ham Factory's use of "Jinhua Ham" on the ham skin is not lawful. The protection of products of origin invoked by the defendant cannot prevail over the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark. The "Regulations on the Protection of Products of Origin" are departmental rules and cannot conflict with the provisions of the Trademark Law. Given the special sales method of ham products and the timing of the defendant's sale of infringing products, the defendant had subjective intent to infringe the plaintiff's right to use its registered trademark. The protection of national brands requires trademark protection as the core, and only the guarantee of the legal system can promote the orderly development of national brands. The defendant Taikang Company argued: It had fulfilled its duty of examining the goods before sale. The trademark "真方宗" on the outer packaging is a registered trademark of Yongkang Ham Factory, and the use of the product of origin name was approved by the relevant state authorities. The "Jinhua Ham" sold by the defendant originated from the Jinhua area and would not mislead consumers or cause infringement of the plaintiff's registered trademark. Yongkang Ham Factory argued: The defendant used "Jinhua Ham" in accordance with the regulations on the protection of products of origin and did not infringe the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark. "Jinhua" is an administrative geographical name, and "Ham" is a generic name for the product; the defendant's use of "Jinhua" constitutes fair use. "Jinhua Ham" is also a distinctive name of a well-known product. "Jinhua Ham" has a history of over 1,200 years, and it would be unfair to allow only the plaintiff to use "Jinhua Ham." The defendant had no subjective intent to infringe the plaintiff's registered trademark.

A product of origin, or geographical indication, refers to an indication that identifies a good as originating from a territory, region, or locality within that territory, where a given quality, reputation, or other characteristic of the good is essentially attributable to its geographical origin. Section 3 of the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights, to which China has acceded, specifically provides for the protection of geographical indications by member states. When China acceded to the World Trade Organization, it undertook to comply with the relevant provisions of the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights regarding geographical indications. Article 16 of the Trademark Law specifically adds provisions for the protection of geographical indications. This Article states: "Where a trademark contains a geographical indication of the goods and the goods do not originate from the region indicated, misleading the public, the trademark shall not be registered and its use shall be prohibited; however, if it has been registered in good faith, it shall continue to be valid. The term 'geographical indication' as used in the preceding paragraph refers to an indication that identifies a good as originating from a region, where a given quality, reputation, or other characteristic of the good is essentially attributable to the natural or human factors of that region." The Implementing Regulations promulgated thereafter, in Article 6, provide that geographical indications may be protected through the application for certification marks and collective marks. On June 7, 2005, the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine issued Order No. 78, publishing the "Regulations on the Protection of Geographical Indication Products."

For a long time, China has attached importance to the protection of products of origin. In order to effectively protect China's products of origin, standardize the use of special marks for products of origin, and protect the quality and characteristics of products of origin, since 1999, the former State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision formulated the "Regulations on the Protection of Products of Origin" and the "General Requirements for Products of Origin," among other regulations, which provide for the definition of products of origin, application authorities, application materials, approval and management authorities, scope of protection, and use of special marks. These series of regulations constitute the legal system for the protection of products of origin in China. Therefore, like other intellectual property rights, products of origin are protected by law in China.

The defendant Yongkang Ham Factory has the right to use the name of the product of origin and the special mark in accordance with the law. The General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine approved the protection of "Jinhua Ham" as a product of origin and agreed that 55 enterprises, including Yongkang Ham Factory, may use the special mark for "Jinhua Ham" as a product of origin. Therefore, Yongkang Ham Factory has the right, in accordance with the relevant national regulations, to mark the product of origin name "Jinhua Ham" and the special mark for products of origin on the outer packaging and labels of the ham products it produces and sells.

Based on the analysis of the facts of this case, first, the defendant Yongkang Ham Factory prominently displayed its registered trademark "真方宗" on the outer packaging of its hams, and also indicated the enterprise name, factory address, contact information, etc. Second, the words "Jinhua Ham" stamped on the skin of the ham by Yongkang Ham Factory were marked below with "Certified by the Origin Management Committee," and the registered trademark "真方宗" was also stamped on the upper part of the ham skin. Therefore, from the above manner of use, it can be determined that the purpose of Yongkang Ham Factory's marking of "Jinhua Ham" was to indicate that the product is a product of origin. Accordingly, the above use of the product of origin name "Jinhua Ham" by Yongkang Ham Factory does not constitute infringement of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark.

The conflict between the trademark right and the product of origin right in this case should be resolved in accordance with the principles of good faith, respect for history, and balance of rights and obligations. From the historical development of "Jinhua Ham," "Jinhua Ham" has a long history, and the formation of the brand embodies the painstaking efforts and wisdom of generations of people in the Jinhua area and related areas. After the plaintiff became the trademark registrant, it has done a great deal of work to enhance the visibility of the trademark. The plaintiff's trademark has repeatedly been awarded honors such as Zhejiang Provincial Famous Trademark, the Gold Medal of the State Bureau of Quality and Technical Supervision, and Zhejiang Provincial Famous Brand Product. The plaintiff's registered trademark should be protected by law. However, on the other hand, the plaintiff, as the holder of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark, has no right to prohibit others from making fair use. Article 49 of the Implementing Regulations provides: "Where a registered trademark contains the generic name, figure, or model of the goods, or directly indicates the quality, main raw materials, functions, uses, weight, quantity, or other characteristics of the goods, or contains a place name, the holder of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark has no right to prohibit others from making fair use thereof." In China, both the exclusive right to use a registered trademark of a rights holder and products of origin are protected by law, and as long as the rights holder uses them in accordance with the relevant regulations, such use is lawful and reasonable. In this case, the defendant Yongkang Ham Factory was approved by the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine to use the product of origin name and the special mark, which is protected by law, and the use by Yongkang Ham Factory does not constitute infringement of the plaintiff's trademark right. The defendant Taikang Company is a seller of Jinhua Ham. Since the conduct of the manufacturer Yongkang Ham Factory does not constitute infringement of the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its trademark, the sales conduct of Taikang Company also does not constitute infringement of the plaintiff's trademark right. Therefore, the plaintiff's request that the two defendants bear the relevant civil liability is not supported.

In conclusion, the resolution of the dispute in this case must strictly comply with existing laws and regulations while also respecting history and promoting a balance of rights and obligations. The core of the scope of protection of the plaintiff Zhejiang Food Company's exclusive right to use its registered trademark is "Jinhua Ham," and its exclusive right is protected by law. Any act infringing upon the plaintiff's exclusive right to use its registered trademark shall bear responsibility according to law. However, the plaintiff has no right to prohibit others from making fair use. "Jinhua Ham" has been approved by the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine for protection as a product of origin, and the defendant Yongkang Ham Factory has been approved to use the special mark for "Jinhua Ham" as a product of origin. Therefore, the above conduct of Yongkang Ham Factory constitutes fair use. Yongkang Ham Factory shall standardize its use of the product of origin in the future. Both the plaintiff and the defendants should respect each other's intellectual property rights and exercise their rights in accordance with the law. The plaintiff's claim that the two defendants infringed its exclusive right to use its registered trademark lacks sufficient basis and is not supported.

Accordingly, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on August 25, 2005:

The plaintiff's claim is dismissed.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 2,375 shall be borne by the plaintiff, Zhejiang Provincial Food Co., Ltd.

After the judgment was rendered, neither party appealed within the statutory period for appeal, and the judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
